{{recipesummary|category=South Asian recipes|servings=4|time=45 minutes|difficulty=3}} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Curry|Curry]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian cuisine]] The original contributor of this recipe left the following comment:
''"My colleague Venayagaratnam ("Sri" from Sri Lanka) gave me this recipe, and I enjoyed it the first time I made it."''
==Ingredients== * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] or other [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]] * 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] * 8 pieces [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] thighs, cut up * 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * 1 clove [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], crushed (see notes) * 1 small piece [[Cookbook:Ginger|fresh ginger]], crushed * 2–3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Tandoori masala|butter chicken masala powder]] * 1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]] ==Procedure== # In a cooking vessel over medium-high heat, add oil and chopped onion, and [[Cookbook:Sauté|sauté]] until light brown. # Add chicken and salt, and leave for 3–5 minutes, stirring in between. # Add crushed ginger and garlic, and stir for 2 minutes. Stir in masala powder, and cook for 2 minutes. # Add water, and let it [[Cookbook:Boil|boil]] for 5 minutes. # Reduce heat to low, and let it cook for 15 minutes, or until the liquid has reduced. == Notes, tips, and variations == * You may substitute 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]] for crushed garlic * "Parampara" butter chicken mix is the recipe's original spice mix found in an Indian food store in North Carolina's Triangle area. [[Category:Recipes using chicken thigh]] [[Category:Recipes for curry]] [[Category:Pan fried recipes]] [[Category:Main course recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using garlic]] [[Category:Recipes using fresh ginger]] [[Category:Recipes using vegetable oil]]
